subject: flamingo
reasoning:
I'm planning out a flamingo model's skeleton and pose with the SDK, thinking through root placement, body loft from tail to chest, and leg joint positions like hip and knee height.

Now I'm detailing the leg chains for hip, knee, ankle, and toe points with thin rod radii, plus feet with webbed forward toes and a small hind toe, and mapping out an S-curve neck chain rising to a bent head and beak. I'm also settling on the color palette: pink body tones, darker legs, a pale beak with a black tip, and folded wings with dark flight-feather edges built from extruded outlines.

Given the T-pose requirement calls for limbs extended, I decide to spread the wings outward and slightly drooped rather than fold them, building them as an arm chain (shoulder-elbow-wrist) with a membrane connecting the leading edge chain to a trailing feather path, using a scalloped edge and a pink-to-black gradient toward the tips.

Writing the paint function and body loft stations...

I need a root joint before a chain can exist, so I'll create a hips joint first, then build a spine chain from it using a short polyline path, and a separate tail chain running from the hips down and back. For the body mesh, I'll loft it rigidly against the hips joint to keep things simple.

Then I'll bind the body loft to both the tail and spine chains together, starting at the tail tip so the spans run correctly front-to-back. The neck will get its own chain parented off the last spine joint, following a curved catmull path upward.

For the neck I'm laying out six control points forming an S-curve from the base of the neck up to the head, giving five joints (neck1 through neck5) plus a head joint at the tip, with a tapering radius function for the sweep.

Now I'm defining the sweep radii as [0.07,0.04,0.028,0.026,0.028] in pink, placing the head as a sphere at the neck tip with eyes at symmetric offset positions, and starting to sketch the upper beak path curving from the head.

Still writing beak and jaw geometry...

Now I'm moving to the legs: for each side I'm setting up hip, knee, and ankle joints, trying to capture the real flamingo leg structure where the visible "knee" is actually the ankle, with the thigh short and forward while the tibiotarsus angles down and back before the tarsus goes down and slightly forward to the foot.

I'm defining the leg chain as a polyline through hip, knee, ankle, and foot points, then sweeping it with a tapering radius profile that's thickest near the thigh and thinnest toward the foot.

Next I'm adding the knobbly ankle joint as a small darker sphere, then building toes as three thin forward-splayed rod bones from the foot joint, plus a flat webbing membrane polygon connecting the toe tips.

Now I'm adjusting toe and leg heights so they sit flush with the floor, adding a short backward hind toe, then moving on to defining the wing structure as a shoulder-elbow-wrist-tip arm chain positioned on the body.

Still defining wing geometry...

Placing feather plumes...

Positioning eyes slightly forward and outward on the head using local offsets, then double-checking overall body proportions so the floor contact points, leg joints, and body loft align sensibly for a flamingo-sized figure.
